overview.text: The Common Gartersnake is one of North America's most widespread snakes, found across most of the non-desert parts of the continent, and it reaches farther north than any other North American snake. It is not dangerous to people and copes with cold better than most snakes.

identification.text: Most have yellowish stripes along a black, brown or green body, but the colours vary a great deal - including green, blue, gold, red and orange forms.

size.label: Adults
size.text: In South Dakota adults measure about 46 to 76 cm (18 to 30 in). Few grow longer than about 1.2 m; the maximum given is about 137 cm.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Much of North America, from the south of Canada through most of the non-desert United States.

behaviour.text: Mostly active by day. It handles colder temperatures than many snakes and may even bask on rocks on mild winter days.

behaviour.label: Winter
behaviour.text: Gartersnakes hibernate in large groups and mate in spring as they come out of their winter dens. In Manitoba, Canada, the huge spring gatherings of the Red-sided Gartersnake at Narcisse draw visitors from around the world.

diet.text: Mainly frogs, toads and salamanders, but a wide range of other prey has been recorded, from earthworms and fish to voles.

funfacts.text: No other North American snake lives as far north as the Common Gartersnake.

ups.title: Common Garter Snake (Thamnophis sirtalis)
ups.publisher: University of Puget Sound Slater Museum
